title: Staggered Traffic Shift Playpad and Communications Runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playpad for a staggered traffic shift (multi-lane) release targeted for mid-June 2026. Focus: predictable ramp, clear comms, quick rollback paths, and short-cycle telemetry checks. Use this during the 72-hour window around the cutover; this is intentionally compact so on-call + SRE can run it from a single screen.

Scope and goals:
- Rollout model/release X (v3.14.0) to hosted + dedicated pools in three waves: internal canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours (configurable).
- Maintain p99 latency target <= 350ms and error rate < 0.5% for user-facing routes.
- No customer data migrations; config-only.

Quick links (open first):
- Jira: REL-512 (launch epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2387
- Telemetry dashboard: Dash: release-telemetry/staggered-shift (runbook widgets)
- Slack channel: #release-512 (watch mode)

Preflight checklist (T-48h -> T-1h)
- [ ] Finalize rollout policy in console: lanes + fallback (owner: Ava)
- [ ] Smoke tests green on canary infra (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Canary model pinned and image digest verified (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Load test baseline (50k rps sim) for 95% traffic envelope (owner: SRE team)
- [ ] Quota and rate-limit adjustments reviewed (owner: Product Ops)
- [ ] Pager escalation rota for the 72h window published to #release-512 (owner: Ellen)
- [ ] Customer-impact list verified; PM sign-off on communications (owner: Samir)

Cutover timeline (day-of snapshot, local timezone UTC-8)
- 08:00 — Preflight sync (15m): on-call, release lead, SRE, infra, PM. Quick readout and go/no-go.
- 08:15 — Canary deploy to 3 internal nodes (manual) — smoke run (10m)
- 08:30 — Telemetry baseline check (15m) — run queries in "telemetry quickchecks" block
- 09:00 — Shift lane A -> 10% public traffic (automated routing)
- 09:30 — Health check and manifest diff verification (15m)
- 10:00 — Shift lane B -> 50% public traffic (if yellow alert, pause)
- 11:00 — Full shift to lane C -> 100% (only after 60m healthy)
- 12:00 — Post-shift stabilization window (2h) — no config changes unless emergency
- 14:00 — Post-deploy retro quickcall (optional)

Telemetry quickchecks (run after each shift step)
- Run these queries in the release dashboard; copy results into #release-512.
  - p99_lat_ms(route="/v1/generate") last 5m < 350ms
  - errors_per_min(route="/v1/generate") last 5m < 0.5% of traffic
  - kv-cache-hit-rate last 10m > baseline -5%
  - tail-quantiles (99.9) spike check: compare to 24h median
- Golden traces: open two request examples (ID sample) and verify no stack mismatch or fatal exceptions.

Signal thresholds & immediate actions
- Severity YELLOW (investigate): p99 >350ms OR error rate >0.5% sustained for 3 consecutive 1m buckets. Actions: pause traffic shift, increase logging-level for affected service, notify SRE.
- Severity RED (rollback candidate): p99 >600ms OR errors >2% OR SLO alerts firing for >5m. Actions: immediate rollback to previous variant (automated policy), start incident bridge, notify infra and product leads.
- If rollout automation fails to apply lanes: manual traffic route via admin console (documented steps below).

Rollback quick guide (if triggered)
1) Pause automated rollout in console (Release -> Active -> Pause).
2) Trigger switch to previous model variant (Release -> rollback -> confirm).
3) Throttle traffic to 30% then 0% if instability persists.
4) Run a targeted canary to confirm healthy state before full restore.
5) Incident bridge: link + summary posted in #incidents and #release-512.

Operational knobs to consider (notes)
- Autoscaling headroom: set scale-up cooldown to 30s for this window to avoid oscillation.
- Batch size & kv-cache retention: prefer conservative profiles for first 24h to limit tail latency risk.
- Quantization toggles: do NOT flip quantization profiles at the same time as rollout. Separate change.

Communications playbook (who says what)
- Internal (Slack):
  - T-1h: pings to #release-512: "Release X starting at 09:00 UTC-8 — on-call: @Diego, SRE: @Priya"
  - On each lane transition: post brief health snippet + link to dashboard
  - On YELLOW: message with next steps and estimated pause time
  - On RED: short incident post with rollback summary and bridge link
- Customer-facing (PM draft) — placeholder to copy into support template: "We rolled out a performance update to our inference endpoint starting June 10. If you observe increased latency, please open a ticket referencing REL-512. We're monitoring and will update at X:XX." (PM to finalize)

Release notes (draft) — copy/paste into changelog after final verification:
- Summary: incremental serving runtime release v3.14.0 — improves multi-session KV cache behavior and reduces tail latency for long context generations.
- Notable changes:
  - Fix: KV cache eviction bug that could cause token duplication at high concurrency (SEE: PR #2387).
  - Perf: improved attention kernel selection for mixed-precision models; p99 improvements expected 7-12% on 8k context.
  - Ops: new routing policy support for staggered-lane rollouts, plus metrics hooks for lane-level telemetry.
- Migration: no customer action required.
- Known issues (pre-cutover):
  - Under rarememory pressure (edge cases), some internal queues may see backpressure; mitigation: scale pool + restart agent (automation in infra runbook).
  - Small probability of a 502 on dedicated pools during the first 10 minutes of a lane shift — SRE to monitor.

Post-deploy checklist (T+0 -> T+72h)
- [ ] 6h health summary posted in #release-512 (owner: Diego)
- [ ] 24h performance comparison (p50/p95/p99) against baseline (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Collect user-facing errors and customer reports, tag with REL-512 (owner: Support)
- [ ] Decide on config opt-in for quantization recommended by Optimize (owner: Product)
- [ ] Final changelog published and release marked "final" in console (owner: Ava)

Notes, loose items, and open questions:
- Q: Should we pre-warm KV caches for Dedicated pools in wave 2? (Priya to advise)
- Q: Add an automated smoke test that runs a small sample of long-context generations after each lane shift? (SRE backlog ticket?)
- TODO: add exact telemetry query snippets to Confluence: Release-Orbits-2026 -> Playpad snippets (linked_artifacts).

Appendix A — admin console quick-steps (manual traffic shift)
1) Console -> Releases -> Select REL-512 -> Edit rollout
2) Toggle lane weights: set target lane to desired % -> Save -> Confirm
3) Observe deployment status; if stuck, check rollout errors in release logs -> escalate to infra.

Appendix B — on-call contact matrix
- Release lead: Ava Chen (pager: ava.chen@redwood.com, slack: @avachen)
- SRE lead: Priya Patel (pager on-call)
- Infra: Diego Marquez
- PM: Samir Gupta

This doc is intentionally terse. If you're running the cutover, copy this playpad to local notes and paste telemetry outputs into #release-512 after each step. Keep edits minimal during the window — favor ephemeral Slack notes for fast comms.

Revision history:
- 2026-06-02: Initial outline (Ava)
- 2026-06-05: Added telemetry quickchecks and thresholds (Priya)
- 2026-06-08: Drafted customer-facing blurb and rollback quick-guide (Ava)
